name: @fjellrute/core
//: There is no build step and no `main`. Both apps compile this package from source: Vite transforms the .ts it resolves through the exports map below, and `tsc -b` type-checks it as a referenced project. A dist/ would mean a stale artefact between an edit here and the app that reads it, which is the drift this package exists to prevent.
//exports: The subpaths are written out one by one rather than as a `./*` wildcard. They are the package's public surface, and a wildcard would make every internal file public — including the adapters' private halves — so a web module could reach past an entry point without anything noticing. It is also what keeps each import in the apps a plain rename of the relative path it replaced, so the module graph and Vite's chunking are unchanged by the extraction.
//peerDependencies: React is a peer, not a dependency: the hooks here must close over the SAME React instance as the app rendering them, and two copies in one tree is the classic 'Invalid hook call' failure. React itself is platform-free — it is React DOM and React Native that are not — so hooks that only fetch and cache data belong here.
